title: NEAR Intents and Chain Signatures: Enhancing Cross-Chain Coordination and Transaction Routing

findings:
NEAR's intent-based system, powered by Chain Signatures and a decentralized Multi-Party Computation (MPC) network, is designed to simplify and enhance cross-chain operations and user interactions. NEAR Intents, launched in November 2024 [S2], coordinate the fulfillment of user requests across different blockchains.

Chain Signatures, a core component of NEAR's cross-chain infrastructure, allows NEAR accounts to sign transactions for any blockchain using a decentralized MPC network [S1, S2, S6]. This infrastructure has processed over $35 billion in all-time cross-chain volume [S1, S7]. The MPC network now operates with 17 independent nodes on mainnet, funded by protocol emissions through the HSP-007 program, enhancing its sustainability and decentralization [S1, S7]. Recent advancements include running all Chain Signatures operations inside Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) for enhanced security and on-chain verifiability [S1, S8]. This TEE integration, combined with encrypted hardware and independent operators, makes the NEAR MPC network a unique and secure solution [S8].

At the protocol level, transactions on NEAR express user intent and are processed through a lifecycle involving receipts [S3, S11]. When a transaction is executed, it generates a receipt that may be routed to different shards for processing, especially for cross-contract calls or transfers to accounts on other shards [S3, S11]. This receipt-based routing mechanism is fundamental to how NEAR handles operations, including those coordinated by NEAR Intents for cross-chain activities [S9]. Chain Signatures enable bridgeless DeFi and multi-chain account abstraction by allowing a single NEAR account to control assets and accounts on other blockchains without intermediaries [S2, S6]. The system supports over 35 networks and can securely add more chains and assets over time [S8].

While the evidence details the infrastructure for transaction routing and cross-chain coordination via intents and Chain Signatures, it does not provide specific details on market microstructure in terms of order books or exchange-specific routing mechanisms. Furthermore, information regarding yield options (e.g., staking APYs, liquid staking protocols, DeFi yields) and hackathons or developer grants is not present in the provided sources.
risk_factors: The security and reliability of the MPC network are critical for Chain Signatures and NEAR Intents, with potential risks associated with node operator collusion or compromise.
Cross-chain transactions coordinated by NEAR Intents are subject to the finality and security mechanisms of both the originating and destination chains, introducing potential delays or complexities.
While TEEs enhance security, reliance on hardware-based trusted execution environments can introduce specific vulnerabilities or trust assumptions.
The decentralization of the MPC network relies on the sustainable operation and incentive alignment of its independent operators.
